target_customer: Software and crypto companies and open-source projects needing continuous security testing (logos shown include Ramp, PostHog, Infisical, Pydantic, Ripple, Phantom)
problem: Human pentests are periodic and costly; Veria Labs runs AI agents that map the attack surface, prove real exploits and draft fix pull requests continuously.
business_model: B2B subscription for continuous AI pentesting (demo-led sales)

founders.name: Stephen Xu
education: Harvey Mudd College, dropped out (per his personal site)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he played on the #1 US CTF team and did computational physics research. His site says he founded the CTF team Les Amateurs.

founders.name: Cayden Liao
prior_employers: Web3 security (fuzzers for crypto and zero-knowledge protocols, employer unnamed)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists NCAA varsity swimmer and #1 US CTF team member; the claim of preventing a 94B USD hack is self-reported and unverified.

founders.name: Jayden Sarveshkumar
founders.background_notes: Does web hacking on the competitive team described as #1 US.

competitors.name: XBOW
competitors.what: Autonomous AI pentesting agents focused on web application vulnerabilities
competitors.traction_then: Reached top of HackerOne US leaderboard with about 1,060 autonomous submissions per its June 2025 write-up as cited by secondary roundups

technical_complexity.rationale: Autonomous exploit discovery and proof that works on real applications is hard and needs elite offensive security skill, though built on foundation models.

defensibility.rationale: Elite hacker team and research reputation help, but XBOW, Horizon3 and others were already shipping and models are available to all.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Well-funded autonomous pentest players already existed; none found acting directly against Veria Labs.

market_need_then: AI generated vulnerability reports were rising fast (HackerOne data cited by a secondary source) and teams shipping AI-written code needed continuous testing; customers shown include several startups and crypto firms.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, direct and technical; short assertive headlines such as Leave nothing to chance

branding.brand_signature: Founded by members of the #1 US competitive hacking team, with public bug research posts
branding.community_and_virality: Public research blog on bugs found in projects such as Aleo, Jolt and Pydantic Monty (company site); a CTFtime team page exists under the Veria Labs name.

brand_strength.rationale: Credibility comes from the hacking team reputation and public research posts, but the name is new and no independent brand press found.

outcome_analysis: Veria Labs, a Fall 2025 company with three founders from a top competitive hacking team, reported a 3.2M USD seed in early 2026 and shows named startup customers. Strong founder skill and the AI security tailwind support it, but XBOW and others are better funded. No negative events found.
notes: Seed of 3.2M reported by StartupHub, TechNews180 and StartupIntros (February 2026); Preqin dates it December 2025. Employbl adds a 500K pre-seed and CB Insights and VCBacked show only 500K, unverified. The competitor source is a 2026 roundup citing XBOW's June 2025 write-up, so the date is secondhand. Name origin not found. Stephen Xu education taken from a search snippet of his personal site.
